description: The DECLARED return type of every semi-structured producer, asserted directly: each expression is projected into a CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT and the created column's type read back, so what is checked is the type the engine hands to a CONSUMER rather than whether some dependent rule happened to fire. Every expectation was measured on a live Snowflake account with two independent instruments that agreed on all of them - SYSTEM$TYPEOF over the expression, and the type the created column receives. Frostlake used to declare all of these VARIANT in the registry and then report the created column VARCHAR. The three families are genuinely distinct static types, not synonyms: OBJECT and ARRAY are refused by the ordering aggregates while VARIANT is accepted, which is why the VARIANT group matters as much as the other two, and the MAP-requiring family refuses an ARRAY exactly as it refuses an OBJECT or a VARIANT. Naming is no guide - OBJECT_KEYS is an ARRAY, ARRAY_MAX is a VARIANT, PARSE_URL is an OBJECT - so every name here was measured, not inferred from a sibling. The expression is projected through a derived table because that is the channel on which the declared type currently travels; both shapes declare the same type on a live account, and the VARCHAR control proves the wrapper does not simply type everything semi-structured. Converted 1:1 from functions/SemiStructuredReturnTypeTest (now retired); the Java helper read the type with DESCRIBE TABLE, which the suite reads from INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS instead so each check is two steps rather than three.
